name: Arithmetic Operators
description: Perform mathematical calculations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, remainder (modulo), and exponentiation.
notes: The + operator also performs string concatenation when either operand is a string.

name: Assignment Operators
description: Assign a value to a variable, optionally combining the assignment with an arithmetic operation on the current value.

name: Comparison Operators (== vs ===)
description: Compare two values. == and != coerce types before comparing, while === and !== check both value and type without coercion.
notes: Best practice is to always use === and !== to avoid unpredictable coercion bugs.

name: Logical Operators (&&, ||, !)
description: Combine or invert boolean expressions. && returns the first falsy value (or the last value), || returns the first truthy value, ! inverts truthiness.
notes: && and || are often used for short-circuit patterns like isReady && doThing() instead of an if statement.

name: Ternary Operator (?:)
description: A shorthand conditional expression that evaluates to one of two values depending on a condition.
notes: Can be chained, but nested ternaries quickly hurt readability — prefer if/else for complex branching.

name: typeof Operator
description: Returns a string indicating the type of the operand, such as 'string', 'number', 'boolean', 'undefined', 'object', or 'function'.
notes: typeof null is 'object' and typeof [] is also 'object' — use Array.isArray() to detect arrays specifically.

name: instanceof Operator
description: Tests whether the prototype of a constructor appears anywhere in an object's prototype chain.
example:
[] instanceof Array; // true
[] instanceof Object; // true
notes: Does not work reliably across different execution contexts (e.g. iframes), where each has its own global constructors.

name: Bitwise Operators
description: Perform operations on the individual bits of numbers: AND, OR, XOR, NOT, left shift, sign-propagating right shift, and zero-fill right shift.
notes: Numbers are converted to 32-bit integers before bitwise operations are applied.

name: Comma Operator
description: Evaluates each of its operands from left to right and returns the value of the last operand.
notes: Rarely used outside of for loop headers, e.g. for (let i = 0, j = 10; i < j; i++, j--).

name: Increment/Decrement Operators (++/--)
description: Increase or decrease a numeric variable by one. The prefix form returns the updated value; the postfix form returns the original value.
example:
let x = 5; x++; // x is 6
let y = 5; console.log(y++); // logs 5, then y is 6

name: Logical Assignment Operators (&&=, ||=, ??=)
syntax: a &&= b   a ||= b   a ??= b
description: Combine a logical operation with assignment, only assigning the right-hand value when the logical condition is met.
example: let config = {}; config.timeout ??= 5000; // sets timeout only if it was null/undefined
notes: Introduced in ES2021 as a concise alternative to patterns like a = a || b.

name: in Operator
description: Tests whether a specified property exists in an object or its prototype chain.
notes: Unlike hasOwnProperty(), in also returns true for inherited properties.

name: delete Operator
description: Removes a property from an object entirely, rather than just setting it to undefined.
example: const obj = { a: 1 }; delete obj.a; 'a' in obj; // false
notes: Has no effect on variables or function declarations — it only removes object properties.

name: void Operator
description: Evaluates an expression and discards its return value, always resulting in undefined.
notes: Historically used in href="javascript:void(0)" links to prevent navigation without producing a visible return value.

name: Exponentiation Operator (**)
description: Raises the first operand to the power of the second operand, equivalent to Math.pow().
